explanation: Perform the first k steps of a uniform shuffle without constructing all n entries. A dictionary records only virtual positions changed by swaps, giving distinct uniformly selected values.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: The map implements the first k swaps of a virtual Fisher–Yates shuffle: unmapped positions still contain their own indices. Each step chooses uniformly from the unselected suffix and moves its chosen value into the result. The ordered sample is uniform; each unordered k-element subset has exactly k! orders, so all subsets have equal probability.
walkthrough: For n=5 and k=2, one possible run chooses virtual position 3, then position 4. It returns [3,4], recording the displaced virtual values only where necessary. Every two-element subset of {0,1,2,3,4} has probability 1/10, regardless of returned order.
edgeCases: k=n returns every value in some order.
No selected value can appear twice.
